# Preface {.unnumbered}

This is an internal METR reference on how open AI labs turn experiments into final training
runs. Each lab chapter uses the same figures, built from `data/*.csv`, so the cross-lab chapter
can overlay them. The scope, lab tiers, and decisions are in the repository README.

**Reading the figures.** Every chapter opens with a scaling curve: training compute on a log
x-axis, loss or a benchmark on the y-axis, experimental runs as dots, the released model(s) as
stars, and a power law fitted to the experiments only, extrapolated out to where the final run
landed. The gap between star and line is how well the lab's experiments predicted its big run.
The compute-split bar under it is the cheap number: what share of logged compute went to
experiments rather than the final run. It is always a lower bound, because failed and unlogged
runs are missing.

**Confidence flags.** Every number in the data carries `reported` (stated by the lab),
`derived` (computed from reported numbers, method in the row), or `guess` (read off a figure).
Chapters state the flag wherever a number changes a conclusion.
